faq.a: Lorem Ipsum is scrambled, pseudo-Latin placeholder text that has been used in publishing and design since the 1500s because its letter distribution looks like normal reading text without being distracting.

faq.q: Can I start with the classic 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' opening?

faq.a: Use the 'Increase / Decrease' tab, enter the starting value and the new value, and the tool shows the percentage change automatically, including whether it's an increase or decrease.

faq.q: How is 'X is what % of Y' calculated?
faq.a: The tool divides X by Y and multiplies by 100, e.g. 25 is what percent of 200 = (25 / 200) × 100 = 12.5%.

faq.q: Is BMI accurate for everyone?
faq.a: BMI is a simple screening measure based on height and weight only. It doesn't account for muscle mass, bone density, age, or sex, so athletes and some other groups may see results that don't reflect their actual body composition.

faq.q: Is this medical advice?
faq.a: No. This tool is for general informational purposes only. Talk to a healthcare professional for advice about your health.

faq.a: In the US, 15–20% is common for restaurant service; norms vary a lot by country, so adjust the slider to whatever fits your situation.

faq.q: Does this calculate tax separately?

faq.q: What is a Unix timestamp?
faq.a: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds (or milliseconds) that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC, widely used by programming languages and databases to represent a point in time.

faq.q: Does this show my local timezone or UTC?
faq.a: Both are shown side by side so you can see the same instant expressed in UTC and in your browser's local timezone.

faq.q: How long should my password be?
faq.a: Most security guidance recommends at least 12–16 characters with a mix of character types for important accounts.

faq.q: What is a UUID?
faq.a: A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a 128-bit identifier that is, for practical purposes, guaranteed to be unique across systems without needing a central authority to issue it.

faq.q: Which UUID version does this generate?
faq.a: This tool generates version 4 UUIDs, which are based on random numbers and are the most common type used in application development.

faq.q: What's the difference between HEX and RGB?
faq.a: HEX and RGB describe the exact same color space — HEX (like #3366FF) is a shorthand hexadecimal encoding of the same red, green, and blue values that RGB expresses as three decimal numbers (like rgb(51, 102, 255)).

faq.q: What is HSL used for?
faq.a: HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) describes color in a way that's often more intuitive for adjusting a color's brightness or intensity while keeping its base hue.

faq.q: Do QR codes generated here expire?
faq.a: No. The QR code encodes your exact text or URL directly (a 'static' QR code), so it works for as long as the destination itself exists — there's no separate service to expire.

faq.q: Can I put a Wi-Fi password or contact card in a QR code?
faq.a: Yes — as long as you format the text using the standard Wi-Fi or vCard syntax, any scanner app that supports those formats will recognize it.
